question: A trader lost 5% by selling a shirt for ₹950. He will gain x% by selling it for ₹1,350. The value of x is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

SP₁ = ₹950 at 5% loss corresponds to 95% of CP.

100% of CP = (950 ÷ 95) × 100 = ₹1000.

New SP₂ = ₹1350.

Gain = SP₂ − CP = 1350 − 1000 = ₹350.

Gain% = (350 ÷ 1000) × 100 = 35%.

**∴ The correct answer is 35%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling price at 5% loss (SP₁) = ₹950

Selling price for x% gain (SP₂) = ₹1350

**Formula Used:**

CP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − Loss%)

Gain% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = (950 × 100) ÷ (100 − 5)

⇒ CP = (950 × 100) ÷ 95 = ₹1000

⇒ New Gain = New SP₂ − CP

⇒ New Gain = 1350 − 1000 = ₹350

⇒ New Gain% = (350 ÷ 1000) × 100

⇒ New Gain% = 35%

⇒ Comparing with x%, we get the value of x as 35.

**∴ The correct answer is 35%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP) & Selling Price (SP)

CP is the price at which a product is purchased. SP is the price at which it is sold. Profit or loss is always calculated on the base of Cost Price unless stated otherwise.

Profit and Loss Formula

Profit = SP − CP, and Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100. Similarly, Loss = CP − SP, and Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always offered on the Marked Price (MP). Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount.
